title: Bounded representatives and bounded roofs in the derived category
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $D^b(R)$ be the bounded derived category of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $K(R)$ for the homotopy category of cochain complexes: its morphisms are chain maps modulo homotopies $f-g=dh+hd$, where $h^n:K^n\to L^{n-1}$. The localization $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(R)\to D(R)$ factors through $K(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Every $C\in D^b(R)$ admits integers $a\le b$, a cochain complex $K$ with $K^n=0$ for $n<a$ or $n>b$, and an isomorphism $C\cong Q(K)$. For bounded representatives $K,L$ of $C,C'$, every $u:C\to C'$ is represented, after transport along those isomorphisms, by a roof $K\xleftarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{g}L$ with $M$ bounded and $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. If $(M_i,s_i,g_i)$, $i=1,2$, are two such roofs with the same endpoints and the same derived morphism, there are a bounded complex $P$ and quasi-isomorphisms $v_i:P\to M_i$ such that $s_1\circ v_1$ is chain homotopic to $s_2\circ v_2$ and $g_1\circ v_1$ is chain homotopic to $g_2\circ v_2$. Thus the roof equivalence is taken in $K(R)$, and the resulting derived morphism is independent of bounded representatives and refinements after transport along the chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 05RW (bounded complexes in the bounded derived category), 05S6 (bounded derived localization), together with the bounded fraction refinements in Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.Fractions.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], $C\in D^b(R)$ has cohomology zero below some $a$ and above some $b$; decrease $a$ or increase $b$ to ensure $a\le b$. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-representative] to $R$-modules to obtain $K$ supported in $[a,b]$ and $C\cong Q(K)$. Do this also for $C'$. This includes zero objects, for which any interval may be used.

For bounded representatives $K,L$, choose $a\le b$ with $K$ supported in $[a,b]$ and $L$ zero below $a$. Transport $u$ along the two specified representative isomorphisms to $f:Q(K)\to Q(L)$. Apply [lem-kun-derived-bounded-roof-factorization] to obtain a bounded $M$ supported in $[a,b]$, $s:M\to K$, $g:M\to L$, and $f=Q(g)\circ Q(s)^{-1}$. The denominator is a quasi-isomorphism: if $Q(s)$ is invertible, each $H^n(Q(s))$ is invertible, and the cohomology functors factor through $Q$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus each $H^n(s)$ is invertible, which is the definition of a quasi-isomorphism.

Suppose $(M_i,s_i,g_i)$ represent the same morphism between $Q(K)$ and $Q(L)$. Work in $K(R)$, not in the category of chain maps. By [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], quasi-isomorphisms in $K(R)$ have a right calculus of fractions and the localization is $D(R)$. Apply [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] in this category. It gives an object represented by a complex $Z$ and chain-map representatives $t_i:Z\to M_i$ such that $s_1t_1=s_2t_2$ and $g_1t_1=g_2t_2$ in $K(R)$, with the common denominator $s_1t_1$ a quasi-isomorphism. The two equalities mean chain homotopies, not strict equalities. No calculus of fractions for quasi-isomorphisms in $\mathrm{CoCh}(R)$ is asserted.

Both $t_i$ are quasi-isomorphisms by the following explicit two-out-of-three calculation. For every $n$, functoriality gives $H^n(s_it_i)=H^n(s_i)H^n(t_i)$. The first factor and the product are isomorphisms; hence $H^n(t_i)=H^n(s_i)^{-1}H^n(s_it_i)$ is an isomorphism. Here the common denominator in Step 3 supplies the product for each $i$. Choose integers $a<b$ so that all four bounded complexes $M_1,M_2,K,L$ vanish outside $[a,b]$. Since $t_1$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $H^n(Z)=0$ outside this interval.

proof.text: Use the existing canonical cochain-complex truncations in Mathlib directly. Put T = tau_LE_b Z, j:T→Z, c=a−1, P=tau_GE_c T and q:T→P. Since t_1 is a quasi-isomorphism and M_1 is strictly supported in [a,b], isSupported_iff_of_quasiIso gives Z.IsLE b and T.IsGE a. The standard quasiIso_ιTruncLE and quasiIso_πTruncGE instances make j and q quasi-isomorphisms. Truncation support instances give P strictly supported in [c,b]. This implements Stacks homology Tag 0118 without importing the composite definition module about truncations, sheaf colimits and sequential homotopy colimits.

proof.text: For r_i=j≫t_i, let v_i=truncGEMap(r_i,c)≫inv(M_i.πTruncGE c). The inverse exists since each M_i is strictly ≥a and hence strictly ≥c. Naturality of πTruncGE gives q≫v_i=r_i. Since q and r_i are quasi-isomorphisms, quasiIso_of_comp_left shows that v_i is a quasi-isomorphism. These are the canonical cokernel-induced factorizations from Stacks homology Tag 0118.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, lower-truncation cokernel formula; explicit factorization

proof.text: Precompose each chain homotopy from the fraction criterion with j. Descend it along q componentwise: for a target N equal to K or L, define H(i,j)=inv(q.f i)≫h(i,j) if c<i, and zero otherwise. Above c, q.f i is invertible by the nonboundary formula for the canonical lower truncation. At i≤c the only possibly nonzero h(i,j) has j+1=i, so N.X j is zero because N is strictly ≥a=c+1. Thus q.f i≫H(i,j)=h(i,j) in all degrees. Each q.f i is epi; cancel it to verify the shape and homotopy equations, using the chain-map equation for q. This gives the two required homotopies for v_1 and v_2. The private helper homotopy_descend_epi proves this calculation in Lean. Transport of arbitrary endpoint isomorphisms is already performed in Step 2.

lean.statement: theorem boundedDerivedRoofs (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} R)] : (Nonempty ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q)) ∧ (∀ (C : DerivedCategory.Bounded (ModuleCat.{v} R)), ∃ (a b : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ), a ≤ b ∧ K.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ K.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ Nonempty (C.1 ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) ∧ (∀ (C C' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ) (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ), K.IsStrictlyGE a → K.IsStrictlyLE b → L.IsStrictlyGE a → L.IsStrictlyLE b → a ≤ b → ∀ (eC : C ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (eC' : C' ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) (u : C ⟶ C'), ∃ (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (_ : M.IsStrictlyGE a) (_ : M.IsStrictlyLE b) (s : M ⟶ K) (_ : QuasiIso s) (g : M ⟶ L), u = eC.hom ≫ inv (DerivedCategory.Q.map s) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map g ≫ eC'.inv) ∧ (∀ (K L M₁ M₂ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (s₁ : M₁ ⟶ K) (g₁ : M₁ ⟶ L) (s₂ : M₂ ⟶ K) (g₂ : M₂ ⟶ L) [hs₁ : QuasiIso s₁] [hs₂ : QuasiIso s₂], (∃ (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b ∧ K.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ K.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ L.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ M₁.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M₁.IsStrictlyLE b ∧ M₂.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M₂.IsStrictlyLE b) → inv (DerivedCategory.Q.map s₁) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map g₁ = inv (DerivedCategory.Q.map s₂) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map g₂ → ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (v₁ : P ⟶ M₁) (v₂ : P ⟶ M₂), (∃ (c d : ℤ), c ≤ d ∧ P.IsStrictlyGE c ∧ P.IsStrictlyLE d) ∧ QuasiIso v₁ ∧ QuasiIso v₂ ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy (v₁ ≫ s₁) (v₂ ≫ s₂)) ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy (v₁ ≫ g₁) (v₂ ≫ g₂)))
